entries.headline: Pacific Imperial ends Brownell Lake option agreement
entries.dek: The company cited a lack of funding after its recent private placement was cancelled, as Eagle Plains Resources agreed to terminate the deal.
entries.caption: A gravel road winds through boreal forest toward a remote mineral claim.

sources.title: Pacific Imperial Announces Cancellation of the Brownell Option Agreement

unverified_claims: The stated reason for the termination — lack of funding following the cancellation of a private placement — rests solely on the company's own characterization; the release does not identify the placement or its terms.
brief: Pacific Imperial Mines Inc. (TSXV: PPM) said it has reached a mutual agreement with Eagle Plains Resources Ltd. to terminate the Option Agreement covering the Brownell Lake VMS project, effective immediately. The company said the termination followed a lack of funding resulting from the recent cancellation of its private placement.

The release gives no further detail on the terms of the original Option Agreement or on the private placement that was cancelled. Pacific Imperial is a Vancouver-based mineral exploration company currently focused on its Babine and Fenton properties in British Columbia.
The company said its board of directors is actively reviewing its strategic options and will re-evaluate how to move forward. No timeline or further disclosure was given.
body: Pacific Imperial Mines Inc. (TSXV: PPM) announced on October 20, 2026 that it has reached a mutual agreement with Eagle Plains Resources Ltd. to terminate the Option Agreement on the Brownell Lake VMS project, effective immediately.

The company said the termination resulted from "a lack of funding resulting from the recent cancellation of its private placement." The release does not identify which placement was cancelled, when, or on what terms, nor does it describe the terms of the original Option Agreement on the Brownell Lake project.
Pacific Imperial said its board of directors is actively reviewing the company's strategic options and will be re-evaluating how to move forward. No timeline was given for that review.

The release describes Pacific Imperial as a Vancouver-based mineral exploration company engaged in the acquisition, exploration, evaluation and development of mineral properties, with its current focus on the Babine and Fenton properties in British Columbia. The disclosure in this release is limited to the termination itself and gives no further operational or financial detail.

entries.headline: S&T Bancorp posts record quarterly earnings per share
entries.dek: The Pennsylvania bank holding company reported $38.6 million in third-quarter net income and continued its share buyback program.
entries.caption: A regional bank branch at dusk, lights on after the trading day has closed.

sources.title: S&T Bancorp, Inc. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

unverified_claims: The characterization of diluted EPS and revenue as 'record' is the company's own description, stated in its release headline and CEO quote.
brief: S&T Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: STBA), the holding company for S&T Bank, reported net income of $38.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $36.6 million in the second quarter and $35.0 million a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share reached $1.09, which the company's release headlined as a record, up 6.9% from the prior quarter.

Net interest margin on a fully taxable equivalent basis expanded seven basis points to 4.06%. Nonperforming assets fell $3.7 million to $36.5 million, or 0.45% of total loans and other real estate owned. Total assets were flat at $9.9 billion, with total borrowings down $60.0 million to $215.3 million.

The company said it has repurchased 3,169,294 shares, 8.3% of shares outstanding, since the fourth quarter of 2025 at an average price of $42.09 per share, and declared a dividend of $0.37 per share. CEO Chris McComish said the quarter reflected "record earnings per share, record revenue and higher core profitability."
body: S&T Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: STBA), the Indiana, Pennsylvania-based holding company for S&T Bank, reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $38.6 million, up from $36.6 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $35.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share was $1.09, which the company said represented a 6.9% increase from the prior quarter and a 19.8% increase from a year earlier, and which its own release headlined as a record.

Profitability measures improved across the board: return on average assets was 1.55%, return on average equity was 10.84%, and return on average tangible shareholders' equity, a non-GAAP measure, was 14.81%. Net interest margin on a fully taxable equivalent basis expanded seven basis points from the prior quarter to 4.06%.

Asset quality metrics moved favorably. Nonperforming assets decreased $3.7 million to $36.5 million, representing 0.45% of total loans plus other real estate owned. Net charge-offs totaled $2.1 million, or 0.10% of average loans. The allowance for credit losses was unchanged at $93.3 million, or 1.16% of total portfolio loans.

On the balance sheet, total assets were flat at $9.9 billion. Total deposits decreased $22.2 million and total borrowings decreased $60.0 million to $215.3 million. Total portfolio loans decreased $4.4 million, which the company attributed to lower line utilization.

S&T Bancorp said it has repurchased 3,169,294 shares, or 8.3% of shares outstanding, since the fourth quarter of 2025, at an average price of $42.09 per share. Approximately 35.3 million shares were outstanding at quarter-end. The company also declared a dividend of $0.37 per share.
CEO Chris McComish said the results reflected "record earnings per share, record revenue and higher core profitability."

entries.headline: Norfolk Southern reports record quarterly revenue
entries.dek: The railroad posted $3.5 billion in third-quarter revenue and diluted earnings per share of $3.37, both up from a year earlier.
entries.caption: A long freight train moves through open countryside as the morning light breaks.

sources.title: Norfolk Southern reports third quarter 2026 results

unverified_claims: The characterization of revenue as a 'quarterly record' is the company's own description.
The operating-ratio comparisons and adjusted figures (excluding merger-related and Eastern Ohio incident costs) are non-GAAP measures as presented by the company.
brief: Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.5 billion, which the company's release called a quarterly record, up $423 million, or 14%, from a year earlier. Income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up 5%, and diluted earnings per share was $3.37, up 7%.

The operating ratio, a measure of operating expenses against revenue, was 67.4%, compared with 64.6% a year earlier. Volume rose 3% year over year. The company said merger-related expenses and costs tied to the Eastern Ohio incident affected the reported figures.

Excluding those items, Norfolk Southern said adjusted income from railway operations was also $1.2 billion, up 7%, with an adjusted operating ratio of 65.4% and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $3.62, up 10%. CEO Mark George called it a quarter of "solid execution."
body: Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 22, 2026. Revenue was $3.5 billion, which the company's release described as a quarterly record, up $423 million, or 14%, from the third quarter of 2025. Income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up $52 million, or 5%. Diluted earnings per share was $3.37, up $0.21, or 7%, from a year earlier.

The operating ratio — the share of revenue consumed by operating expenses, where a lower figure indicates greater efficiency — was 67.4% for the quarter, compared with 64.6% in the third quarter of 2025. The company said volume increased 3% year over year.

Norfolk Southern also reported adjusted results that it said exclude merger-related expenses and the effects of the Eastern Ohio incident. On that adjusted basis, income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, with an adjusted operating ratio of 65.4%.
Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $3.62, up 10% from the third quarter of 2025.
CEO Mark George said: "Norfolk Southern delivered another quarter of solid execution, with record revenues, and strong earnings growth."

The release described Norfolk Southern's network as spanning 22 states and moving approximately 7 million carloads annually, operating what it called the most extensive intermodal network in the eastern United States, and said rail transport helps its customers avoid approximately 15 million tons of carbon emissions each year.
